[[Request stop|Flag stop]] (''City of New Orleans'') | accessible = | code = {{Amtrak code|KKI}} | zone = | mpassengers = {{rail pass box|system=Amtrak|passengers={{Amtrak ridership|Kankakee}}{{Amtrak ridership|citationIL}}|pass_year={{Amtrak ridership|date}}}} | services = {{Adjacent stations|system1=Amtrak |line1=City of New Orleans|left1=Champaign-Urbana|right1=Homewood |line2=Saluki/Illini|left2=Gilman|right2=Homewood}} | other_services_header = Former services | other_services_collapsible = yes | other_services = {{Adjacent stations| |system4=Illinois Central Railroad |line4=main|left4=Otto|right4=Bradley }} | nrhp = {{Infobox NRHP | embed = yes | name = Illinois Central Railroad Depot | image = | caption = | location = [[Kankakee, Illinois]], USA | nearest_city = | coordinates = {{coord|41|7|9.48|N|87|51|56.16|W|display=inline,title}} | mapframe = yes | mapframe-custom = {{Infobox mapframe |shape=none |marker=rail |marker-color=#{{rcr|Amtrak}} |zoom=14 }} | area = | built = 1898 | architect = | architecture = | added = April 28, 2000 | refnum = 00000409 | visitation_num = | visitation_year = | governing_body = }} }} '''Kankakee station''' is an [[Amtrak]] intercity train station in [[Kankakee, Illinois]], United States. The station is a regular stop for the ''[[Illini and Saluki]],'' and is a [[flag stop]] for the ''[[City of New Orleans (train)|City of New Orleans]]'', served only when passengers have tickets to and from the station. The present station was built by the [[Illinois Central Railroad]] in 1897. == History == The [[Illinois Central Railroad]] Company was founded in 1851. By 1853, newly founded Kankakee was connected [[Chicago]], {{convert|56|mi}} away. The first train pulled into the station on July 11, 1853. The rail connection reduced the travel time between the two cities from six days by wagon to three hours by rail. It also provided Kankakee with access to industrial resources in the north–south direction; the city was no longer dependent on the east–west [[Kankakee River]]. Kankakee was incorporated two years later.[https://web.archive.org/web/20131203044752/http://gis.hpa.state.il.us/pdfs/205581.pdf Illinois Historic Preservation Agency] The original station was a small, wood-framed station. However, by the 1890s, it had fallen into disrepair and no longer conformed to city ordinances. The Illinois Central agreed to commission a new train station in 1897, which was completed the next year. The first train arrived at the new station at 7:30 a.m. on January 10, 1898. [[Frank Lloyd Wright]] traveled through the station on several occasions while designing two houses in Kankakee, remarking of the new building, "not a style of my choosing but good enough for the community." The city was also served by the [[New York Central Railroad]] at another station, with trains such as the ''[[James Whitcomb Riley (train)|James Whitcomb Riley]],'' bound for Cincinnati. Telephones were installed in 1902, replacing the original telegraph wires. These lines were moved underground in 1911. Rail use declined in the 1930s, coinciding with the [[Great Depression]] and the increased use of automobiles. Furthermore, the [[Kankakee Electric Railway Company]], which provided interurban service to the station, went out of business in 1933. The station saw a resurgence in the 1940s during [[World War II]], when personnel training at [[Chanute Field]] in [[Rantoul, Illinois|Rantoul]] would come to Kankakee on leisure time. The station has remained in continuous use since 1898. == Historical services == Historically, the station served trains on the Illinois Central's routes going southwest, south and southeast. The last of these, aside from the ''City of New Orleans,'' ''Illini'' and ''Saluki'' was the ''South Wind.''''Official Guide of the Railways,'' December 1957, Illinois Central section to St. Louis: *''[[Green Diamond]]'' to New Orleans: *''[[City of New Orleans (train)|City of New Orleans]]'' *''[[Panama Limited]]'' to Florida: *''[[Seminole (train)|Seminole]]'' *''[[South Wind (train)|South Wind]]'' == Disposition today == The station has been on the [[National Register of Historic Places listings in Kankakee County, Illinois|National Register of Historic Places]] since the year 2000.[http://www.nationalregisterofhistoricplaces.com/IL/Kankakee/state.html Kankakee County Listings at the National Register of Historic Places] By the late 1980s, the depot had fallen into disrepair. The city purchased the building from the Illinois Central in 1990 and finished a full restoration eight years later. The $1 million project was funded with $750,000 in city funds and private donations.[http://www.greatamericanstations.com/Stations/KKI/Station_view Great American Stations]. Accessed March 27, 2013. Today, the northern end of the station is home of the Kankakee Railroad Museum.{{cite web|title=Welcome|url=http://www.kankakeerrmuseum.com/|publisher=Kankakee Railroad Museum|access-date=29 May 2011|year=2011}} == In popular culture == In Steve Goodman's song "[[City of New Orleans (song)|City of New Orleans]]" (popularized by [[Arlo Guthrie]]) the train departs the Kankakee station. == Bus Connections == '''[[River Valley Metro]]:''' – Routes 1, 7, & 8 == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == {{commonscat-inline|Kankakee station}} {{Amtrak web|KKI|Kankakee, IL}} *[http://www.trainweb.org/usarail/kankakee.htm Kankakee Amtrak Station (USA Rail Guide -- Train Web)] {{Amtrak Illinois stations}} [[Category:Amtrak stations in Illinois]] [[Category:Transportation in Kankakee County, Illinois]] [[Category:Kankakee, Illinois]] [[Category:Railway stations on the National Register of Historic Places in Illinois]] [[Category:Railway stations in the United States opened in 1898]] [[Category:Former Illinois Central Railroad stations]] [[Category:National Register of Historic Places in Kankakee County, Illinois]]
